One bank skipped one job. The fine: $1.2 billion.
On Oct 13, 2026, the US Treasury (FinCEN) assessed a $1.2B penalty on Bank of America; the OCC's record $750M penalty counts toward it.
Treasury says over $5B in suspicious transactions went unreported or reported late, over $1B tied to national-security risks. The bank admitted willfully violating the Bank Secrecy Act, and its Q3 2026 results (Oct 14) show the charge cut EPS by $0.17.
It's FinCEN's third-largest penalty, behind Binance (2023) and TD Bank (2024). Separately, banks report cash moves over $10,000 a day as routine paperwork.
Sources: US Treasury and FinCEN (Oct 13, 2026), CNBC, CNN, Newsweek.
News and education, not financial advice.
Follow @financeprostv for money explained simply.
